area: CLAUDE.md, memory, rule files, path scoping, imports, /doctor, /init, managed CLAUDE.md, auto-memory

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md vs auto memory (two memory systems)
facts.behavior: Claude Code has two complementary memory systems. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation. Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration. To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, use a PreToolUse hook instead. The more specific and concise your instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.
facts.limits: CLAUDE.md: instructions/rules you write, scope project/user/org, loaded every session. Auto memory: learnings/patterns Claude writes itself, scope per repository shared across worktrees, loaded every session but only the first 200 lines or 25KB of MEMORY.md.

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md files are markdown files that give Claude persistent instructions for a project, your personal workflow, or your entire organization. You write these files in plain text; Claude reads them at the start of every session.
facts.limits: Keep it to facts Claude should hold in every session: build commands, conventions, project layout, 'always do X' rules. If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase, move it to a skill or a path-scoped rule instead.

facts.behavior: Organizations can deploy a centrally managed CLAUDE.md that applies to all users on a machine, at macOS `/Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md`, Linux/WSL `/etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md`, or Windows `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md`. Scope: every Claude Code session on the machine, in every repository. Precedence: loads before user and project CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: This file cannot be excluded by individual settings; managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded by `claudeMdExcludes`. The `claudeMd` key can alternatively put managed CLAUDE.md content directly inside `managed-settings.json`; setting `claudeMd` in user, project, or local settings has no effect (honored only in managed/policy settings).

facts.behavior: Personal preferences for all projects (code styling preferences, personal tooling shortcuts), shared with just you across all projects.
facts.limits: Loaded at launch; appears in context before project instructions (order is broadest scope to most specific).

facts.behavior: Team-shared instructions for the project (project architecture, coding standards, common workflows), shared with team members via source control.
facts.limits: Create instructions that apply to anyone working on the project; focus on project-level standards rather than personal preferences. To confirm the file loaded, run `/context` and check the list under Memory files.

facts.behavior: Personal project-specific preferences (your sandbox URLs, preferred test data); loads alongside CLAUDE.md and is treated the same way; shared with just you (current project).
facts.limits: Should be added to `.gitignore` so it isn't committed. If you work across multiple git worktrees of the same repository, a gitignored CLAUDE.local.md only exists in the worktree where you created it; to share personal instructions across worktrees, import a file from your home directory instead (e.g. `@~/.claude/my-project-instructions.md`).

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md load order and concatenation across directory hierarchy
facts.behavior: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md from your current working directory and every directory above it. All discovered files are concatenated into context rather than overriding each other. Across the directory tree, content is ordered from the filesystem root down to your working directory, so instructions closer to where you launched Claude are read last. Within each directory, CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md, so your personal notes are the last thing Claude reads at that level.
facts.limits: Files in subdirectories under the working directory are not loaded at launch; instead they are included on demand when Claude reads files in those subdirectories.

facts.behavior: The `--add-dir` flag gives Claude access to additional directories outside the main working directory. To also load memory files from these directories, set `CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1`. This loads `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/*.md`, and `CLAUDE.local.md` from the additional directory.
facts.limits: By default, CLAUDE.md files from `--add-dir` directories are NOT loaded. `CLAUDE.local.md` is skipped if you exclude `local` from `--setting-sources`.

facts.behavior: Block-level HTML comments (`<!-- maintainer notes -->`) in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context. Use them to leave notes for human maintainers without spending context tokens on them.
facts.limits: Comments inside code blocks are preserved (not stripped). When you open a CLAUDE.md file directly with the Read tool, comments remain visible (only stripped for context injection).

facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md files can import additional files using `@path/to/import` syntax. Imported files are expanded and loaded into context at launch alongside the CLAUDE.md that references them. Both relative and absolute paths are allowed; relative paths resolve relative to the file containing the import, not the working directory. Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops.
facts.limits: Import parsing skips Markdown code spans and fenced code blocks, so wrapping a path in backticks (e.g. `` `@README` ``) keeps it literal instead of importing it. Splitting into @path imports helps organization but doesn't reduce context, since imported files still load and enter the context window at launch.

facts.behavior: An import in a project-level memory file is external when its path resolves outside your working directory (e.g. a home-directory import). The first time Claude Code encounters external imports in a project, it shows an approval dialog listing the files. If you decline, the imports stay disabled and the dialog doesn't appear again. User-scope memory files (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.claude/rules/`) load their imports without the dialog and are trusted like the rest of personal configuration.
facts.limits: Exception: in Cowork sessions on desktop, Claude Code skips any import in a user-scope file that resolves outside the session's working directory (loading the rest of the file), and also skips a `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` that is itself a symlink/hard link, and a symlinked `~/.claude/rules/` directory or rule file pointing outside the working directory.

facts.behavior: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md. If a repo already uses AGENTS.md, create a CLAUDE.md that imports it (`@AGENTS.md`) so both tools read the same instructions; Claude-specific instructions can be appended below the import. A symlink (`ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md`) also works if no Claude-specific content is needed (not on Windows without admin/Developer Mode, where the @AGENTS.md import must be used instead).
facts.limits: Claude does not natively read AGENTS.md without an import or symlink pointing CLAUDE.md at it.

facts.behavior: Run `/init` to generate a starting CLAUDE.md automatically. Claude analyzes the codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers. If a CLAUDE.md already exists, `/init` suggests improvements rather than overwriting it. `/init` also reads Cursor rules (`.cursor/rules/` or `.cursorrules`) and Copilot rules (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) and incorporates relevant parts into the generated CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: With `CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1` set, an interactive multi-phase flow is enabled instead: `/init` asks which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks), explores the codebase with a subagent, fills gaps via follow-up questions, and presents a reviewable proposal before writing files; in this mode it also reads AGENTS.md, `.devin/rules/`, `.windsurf/rules/` or `.windsurfrules`, and `.clinerules`.

facts.behavior: Run `/import` to bring a supported coding agent's configuration into Claude Code, which appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as AGENTS.md to the matching CLAUDE.md and carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents, and skills.
facts.limits: Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later.

facts.behavior: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence. Use markdown headers and bullets to group related instructions. Write instructions concrete enough to verify, e.g. 'Use 2-space indentation' instead of 'Format code properly', 'Run `npm test` before committing' instead of 'Test your changes'.
facts.limits: If instructions grow large, use path-scoped rules so they load only when Claude works with matching files.

facts.behavior: If two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily. Review CLAUDE.md files, nested CLAUDE.md files, and .claude/rules/ periodically to remove outdated or conflicting instructions.
facts.limits: No automatic conflict detection or resolution mechanism is described.

facts.behavior: Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md file of up to 4 MiB in full and skips a larger file. Shorter files produce better adherence.
facts.limits: Applies per CLAUDE.md file (not the 200-line/25KB limit, which is specific to auto memory's MEMORY.md).

facts.behavior: For larger projects, instructions can be organized into multiple files using the .claude/rules/ directory, one topic per file (e.g. testing.md, api-design.md). All .md files are discovered recursively, so rules can be organized into subdirectories. Rules without `paths` frontmatter are loaded at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md.
facts.limits: Project rules are skipped if `project` is excluded from `--setting-sources`. Before v2.1.211, rules that load on demand (path-scoped rules and rules in nested .claude/rules/ directories) loaded even when `project` was excluded (bug, since fixed).

facts.behavior: Rules can be scoped to specific files using YAML frontmatter with a `paths` field (glob patterns). These conditional rules only apply when Claude is working with files matching the specified patterns. Rules without a `paths` field are loaded unconditionally and apply to all files. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude reads files matching the pattern, not on every tool use. As of v2.1.198, matching also works when Claude reaches a file through a symlinked path to the project directory.
facts.limits: Multiple patterns and brace expansion supported (e.g. `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`). A rule's whole `paths` list shares one budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB; patterns without braces don't count against it. A pattern exceeding the budget is used unexpanded (its literal braces match no files). Before v2.1.217 this stalled/crashed the CLI. A `paths` pattern with an unmatched `[` is invalid, matches nothing (other patterns in the rule still work); before v2.1.207 one invalid pattern broke the Read tool for every file the rule evaluated.

facts.feature: Share rules across projects with symlinks
facts.behavior: The .claude/rules/ directory supports symlinks, so a shared set of rules can be maintained and linked into multiple projects (files or whole directories). Symlinks are resolved and loaded normally; circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully.
facts.limits: N/A beyond symlink resolution described.

facts.behavior: Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on the machine; used for preferences that aren't project-specific. User-level rules are loaded before project rules, giving project rules higher priority.
facts.limits: Same paths-frontmatter scoping mechanics apply as project rules.

facts.behavior: In large monorepos, `claudeMdExcludes` lets you skip specific CLAUDE.md files (or rules) by path or glob pattern, matched against absolute file paths. Can be configured at user, project, local, or managed policy settings layer; arrays merge across layers. To exclude a rules file reached via symlink, a pattern matching either the file's path under .claude/rules/ or its link target excludes the file (before v2.1.239, only a pattern matching the link target worked).
facts.limits: Managed policy CLAUDE.md files cannot be excluded by claudeMdExcludes, ensuring organization-wide instructions always apply.

facts.feature: Managed CLAUDE.md vs managed settings (division of concerns)
facts.behavior: Settings rules (e.g. permissions.deny, sandbox.enabled, env, forceLoginMethod/forceLoginOrgUUID) are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides to do. Managed CLAUDE.md is for behavioral guidance: code style/quality guidelines, data handling/compliance reminders, behavioral instructions for Claude.
facts.limits: Managed CLAUDE.md instructions shape Claude's behavior but are not a hard enforcement layer, unlike settings.permissions.deny etc.

facts.behavior: Auto memory lets Claude accumulate knowledge across sessions without you writing anything. As it works, Claude saves four kinds of notes for itself, recorded as a `type` field in the memory file's frontmatter: `user` (role, expertise, working preferences), `feedback` (corrections/confirmed approaches), `project` (ongoing work, deadlines, decisions Claude can't derive from code/git history), `reference` (where to find outside information, e.g. issue tracker or dashboard). Claude doesn't save something every session; it decides what's worth remembering based on future usefulness.
facts.limits: Claude skips anything it can derive from the codebase (architecture, file paths, debugging fixes) and anything CLAUDE.md files already say.

facts.behavior: Auto memory is on by default. Toggle via `/memory` (auto memory toggle), which saves `autoMemoryEnabled` to `~/.claude/settings.json`. To disable for a single project, set `autoMemoryEnabled: false` in that project's settings. To disable via environment variable, set `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`.
facts.limits: N/A

facts.behavior: Each project gets its own memory directory at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/`. `<project>` is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories within the same repo share one auto memory directory (outside a git repo, the project root is used instead). Auto memory is machine-local; files are not shared across machines or cloud environments.
facts.limits: If `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` is set beside `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, that name is used as `<project>` instead, so projects launched with that config directory share one auto memory directory regardless of repository (requires v2.1.234+). `autoMemoryDirectory` setting can override the location (must be absolute path or start with `~/`; honored under the same workspace trust rule as hooks when set in project .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json).

facts.feature: Auto memory retention (excluded from transcript cleanup)
facts.behavior: Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after the `cleanupPeriodDays` retention period, but excludes the files in the memory directory from that retention sweep. MEMORY.md and topic files stay until you or Claude edits or deletes them.
facts.limits: Applies specifically to files in the auto-memory directory, not other session data.

facts.behavior: The memory directory contains a MEMORY.md index (one line per memory) and one topic file per memory. The first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation; content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start. After Claude writes to MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures it against the limits: if near a limit it reminds Claude to shorten it (one line per entry, move detail to topic files, merge/drop stale entries); if over a limit, the write still succeeds but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load.
facts.limits: This 200-line/25KB limit applies only to MEMORY.md, not to individual topic files (user_role.md, feedback_testing.md, etc.), which are not loaded at startup — Claude reads them on demand via standard file tools when needed.

facts.behavior: When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a `modified` frontmatter field as an ISO 8601 timestamp, showing how current the fact is to both user and Claude.
facts.limits: Any file that has frontmatter gets the field the next time Claude writes it, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none. Requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later.

facts.behavior: The main conversation's auto memory isn't loaded into subagents. The exception is a fork, which inherits the parent conversation and system prompt. A subagent's own auto memory, enabled with the subagent `memory` field, is a separate directory.
facts.limits: Non-fork subagents do not see the parent's auto memory at all.

facts.behavior: Lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, and other memory file locations across user and project scopes, including entries for files that don't exist yet. Lets you toggle auto memory on/off and provides an option to open the auto memory folder. Selecting a file opens it in your editor; selecting one that doesn't exist creates it first.
facts.limits: GUI editors (e.g. VS Code) open the file in a separate window and let you keep using the session while open (before v2.1.216, /memory waited for the file to close). Terminal editors (e.g. Vim) take over the terminal until exit. To check which files actually loaded into the current session, use `/context` instead.

facts.feature: Asking Claude to remember something in chat
facts.behavior: When you ask Claude to remember something, like 'always use pnpm, not npm' or 'remember that the API tests require a local Redis instance,' Claude saves it to auto memory. To add instructions to CLAUDE.md instead, ask Claude directly ('add this to CLAUDE.md') or edit the file yourself via /memory.
facts.limits: N/A

facts.feature: CLAUDE.md delivery mechanism and compliance guarantee
facts.behavior: CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message after the system prompt, not as part of the system prompt itself. Claude reads it and tries to follow it, but there's no guarantee of strict compliance, especially for vague or conflicting instructions.
facts.limits: For instructions that must run at a specific point (e.g. before every commit, after each file edit), use a hook instead — hooks execute as shell commands at fixed lifecycle events and apply regardless of what Claude decides to do. For system-prompt-level instructions use `--append-system-prompt` (must be passed every invocation).

facts.behavior: The InstructionsLoaded hook can be used to log exactly which instruction files are loaded, when they load, and why — useful for debugging path-specific rules or lazy-loaded files in subdirectories.
facts.limits: N/A

facts.behavior: The /doctor checkup proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase (directory layouts, dependency lists, architecture overviews) and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults.
facts.limits: The trim check requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.

facts.behavior: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction: after /compact, Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it into the session. Nested CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories and rules with paths: frontmatter reload as Claude reads files they apply to.
facts.limits: If an instruction disappeared after compaction, it was given only in conversation, lives in a nested CLAUDE.md that hasn't reloaded yet, or is a path-scoped rule that hasn't matched a file since. Add conversation-only instructions to CLAUDE.md to make them persist.

facts.behavior: Use @ to quickly include files or directories without waiting for Claude to read them (e.g. 'Explain the logic in @src/utils/auth.js'). @ file references add CLAUDE.md in the file's directory and parent directories to context. Directory references show file listings, not contents. @ can also reference MCP resources using @server:resource format.
facts.limits: File paths can be relative or absolute; typing @ opens a path suggestion menu (Enter/Tab to accept). Multiple files can be referenced in one message.

facts.feature: Work in notes and non-code folders (.claude/ and CLAUDE.md coexistence)
facts.behavior: The .claude/ directory and CLAUDE.md sit alongside other tools' config directories without conflict. Claude reads files fresh on each tool call, so it sees edits made in another application the next time it reads that file.
facts.limits: N/A
